subject: Post-call: Embeddings integration & migration plan

Subject: Post-call: Embeddings integration & migration plan

Hi Rebecca / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo and the detailed call earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before we hand off to engineering: 

Recap (from our understanding)
- Use case: semantic search + reranking for patient-facing knowledge base and internal provider search.
- Current provider: Pinecone (small pilot) with 1536-dim OpenAI embeddings.
- Data: ~1.2M documents (mixed-length notes and PDFs), expect ~10k daily new vectors.
- SLOs: sub-200ms tail for simple query path; batch reindexing can be higher latency.

Open questions we promised to confirm:
1) Target vector dimensionality and whether you want to preserve existing embeddings (migration strategy).
2) Expected query throughput (QPS) and preferred batching window for bulk reindexing.
3) Any normalization/metadata rules you currently apply (L2 norm, per-doc metadata fields).
4) Auth / network constraints for SDK and private deployment (VPC firewall, IP allowlist).

Proposed next steps:
- Technical follow-up: schedule a 30–45m deep-dive with Dev to align on SDK setup, auth flow, and migration options (re-embed vs vector import).
- We’ll share a short migration plan (attached) and an SDK snippet for your platform.
- If you want, we can run a small pilot (10k vectors import + sample queries) to compare ranking differences.

I've attached a short migration plan and a sample SDK snippet. Dev, can you confirm recommended dims, normalization, batching guidance, and a high-level migration path so I can turn this into an actionable plan for Acme?

Thanks —

Thanks Marissa — this is great, and appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Current stack: Pinecone (hosted), embeddings produced by OpenAI ada-002 -> 1536 dimensions. We store per-doc metadata (doc_id, source, timestamp, author).
- Query load: currently ~30 QPS peak for search, expecting to grow to ~150 QPS over next 6–12 months.
- Batch reindex: monthly full reindex plus daily delta (expect 8–12k new vectors daily). We typically perform bulk uploads in 1000–5000 vector batches.
- Normalization: we currently L2-normalize vectors on insert and store raw floats in Pinecone.

Questions: 
1) If we want to preserve historical vectors (not re-embed everything), do you support a direct vector import (raw floats) and any caveats for dimensionality/format?
2) For reranking, we use a two-stage flow (ANN search -> model reranker). Any best practices for embeddings to reduce reranker recall issues?
3) SDK/auth: we need to understand if we can do server-side key exchange via our KMS and if Redwood supports IP allowlists for your hosted endpoints (or whether private deployment is required).

Happy to hop on the technical follow-up — Tom (CC) will own infra side and can join.

Best,
Rebecca Lane
Lead Product Manager, Search | Acme Health

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Lane <rebecca.lane@acmehealth.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Embeddings integration & migration plan

Hi Rebecca / Tom — looping in Neha (solutions engineering) and answering the specific questions below. Short version up top, details after.

TL;DR:
- Yes: Redwood supports direct vector imports (raw float arrays) and hosted ingestion; however, beware of metric differences if you switch kernels/quantization — we recommend validating on a sample set.
- Dimensionality: you can keep 1536. If you move to a different model (e.g., smaller dims) we recommend re-embedding for consistency; otherwise store the dimension as metadata and ensure indexing config matches.
- Normalization: L2-normalized vectors are fine; Redwood supports both normalized and non-normalized vectors. For Cosine-based ANN indexes we prefer normalized vectors at insert time.
- Batching: For bulk reindex, 1k–5k per request is reasonable; RD latency for batches is lower with 2k–4k typical. For live inserts, aim for micro-batches (100–500) if possible.
- Reranker best-practices: use a recall-oriented ANN threshold (higher recall) so the reranker has diverse candidates; store and pass back raw score/metadata to the reranker. Consider using embeddings with context window tuned to the reranker model.

Details / Migration options:
1) Direct import (recommended if you want to avoid re-embedding):
   - Export vectors from Pinecone as float arrays + metadata (doc_id, timestamp, source).
   - Ensure all vectors have identical dimensionality (1536). If any legacy vectors are shorter/padded, reject or pad appropriately.
   - If you L2-normalize in Pinecone, you can import already-normalized vectors. For cosine searches we index expecting normalized input — set index.metric=cosine.
   - Run a small pilot: import 10k vectors, run 100 representative queries, compare top-10 overlap and reranker downstream quality.

2) Re-embed option (recommended if you plan to change model family):
   - Re-embed source documents with the new model (batch re-embed job).
   - Use a canary subset to measure reranker and ranking metrics prior to full cutover.

3) Hybrid approach:
   - Import existing vectors and concurrently re-embed new content. For older content, schedule background re-embed jobs prioritized by traffic.

Technical notes / SDK & Auth:
- SDK setup: We have a Node + Python SDK. Example (Node) for import:

  const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
  await client.vectors.upsert({ index: 'acme-kb', vectors: batch });

- Auth: Hosted API supports server-side API keys, and you can put keys behind your KMS (rotate regularly). For IP allowlist and VPC-only access, we recommend Redwood Private or a Dedicated plan — we can provide an allowlist for certain endpoints but full VPC isolation requires Private.
- Network: If you need egress restrictions for calls to our hosted embedding model endpoints, we can route through regional endpoints; otherwise Private gives full inside-network control.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short SDK sample (js) and a migration checklist. Neha, can you provide the suggested pilot configuration and the perf numbers (latency targets / batch sizes) we'll commit to for the POC?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
